message.content:
The two triangles share the vertical side of length \(h\).

In the left triangle:
- Hypotenuse \(= 2\sqrt{3}\)
- Angle \(= 30^\circ\)
- The vertical side is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, so
\[
h = (2\sqrt{3})\sin 30^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac12 = \sqrt{3}.
\]

In the right triangle:
- The vertical side is \(\sqrt{3}\)
- The angle at the right base is \(45^\circ\)
- Since one angle is \(45^\circ\), it is a \(45^\circ\!-\!45^\circ\!-\!90^\circ\) triangle, so the horizontal leg is also \(\sqrt{3}\).

Thus the hypotenuse \(x\) is
\[
x = \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2+(\sqrt{3})^2}
= \sqrt{3+3}
= \sqrt{6}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\sqrt{6}}\).
